Dear Dr. Morrison,

Thank you for agreeing to assess this male infant, who was noted to have dysmorphic and neuromuscular features evident from birth. 

On craniofacial examination, he displays an expressionless, fixed facies with a distinctly triangular shape. His eyes are widely spaced, showing shortened horizontal palpebral apertures and an inward rolling of the lower eyelid margins. The nasal bridge is conspicuously broad, and the nostrils are stenotic. His ears are situated below the bi-orbital line, though they demonstrate well-preserved helical architecture rather than simplified auricles. Ophthalmic evaluation confirmed clear crystalline lenses without opacities.

The infant demonstrates marked, generalized muscular floppiness with significant head lag. His cutaneous exam is notable for redundant, loose skin that gathers in excessive folds. Orthopedic assessment revealed a dislocated left femoral head, yet all peripheral joints have full passive mobility without fixed contractures, and his feet show normal alignment without clubbing deformities. The spine is completely straight without scoliosis or kyphosis. His hands show dual transverse palmar creases bilaterally. Growth parameters are proportionate, with standard crown-heel length rather than excessive height.

Echocardiography identified an isolated defect within the interventricular septum; the interatrial septum is closed, ventricular wall thickness is normal, and the ascending aorta shows neither caliber dilation nor vascular tortuosity. Genitourinary examination demonstrated normal stretched phallic size, bilateral intrascrotal testes, and clear groins without herniation. Neuroimaging confirmed normal caliber and thickness of the corpus callosum. 

The parents are healthy and non-consanguineous, and routine newborn laboratory screens were unremarkable. I would greatly value your comprehensive assessment and recommendations.

Sincerely,
Dr. Evelyn Vance, MD
